headline: South Asia: Sanaa, Riyadh rattled by strikes as war widens
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Sanaa, Riyadh rattled by strikes as war widens.
- India: Yemeni govt strikes Houthis as tensions rise amid reports of planned Saudi offensive.
- Asia: Houthis say they struck Aramco oil facility, as Saudis hit Sanaa.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Naval Special Warfare Command failed to identify, treat TBI in service members: Watchdog.
- Military Times, one day ago: Naval Special Warfare Command failed to identify, treat TBI in service members: Watchdog.
The DOD Inspector General found that Naval Special Warfare Command failed to identity and treat traumatic brain injuries in personnel.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Marine Corps plans new warfighter test for future generals.
Following Pentagon guidelines, the Marine Corps is developing and testing its own Joint Warfighter Evaluation.
The Caribbean - bottom line: UDC warns it cannot guarantee daily services at Little Dunn’s River.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 22 hours ago: UDC warns it cannot guarantee daily services at Little Dunn’s River.
The Urban Development Corporation (UDC) says the relevant team has been directed to take steps to facilitate public access to Little Dunn’s River Beach in Ocho Rios, St Ann, in compliance with a court order. However, the UDC indicated that it was not in a position at this time to provide “day-to-day management” of the popular recreational spot, including arrangements for security, lifeguard services, sanitation, maintenance or other amenities ordinarily required for such a facility. The UDC is the state entity that owns the facility.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 22 hours ago: Docs to decide on next steps in response to delayed IDT ruling.
More than 100 junior doctors at the Mandeville Regional Hospital in Manchester stayed off the job on Friday, joining hundreds of colleagues across the island. The junior doctors abstained from work in an effort to pressure the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) to give a ruling in its overtime and incentive dispute with the Government or outline a timeline for its award.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Sanaa, Riyadh rattled by strikes as war widens.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Sanaa, Riyadh rattled by strikes as war widens.
• Houthis say Saudi aircraft carried out 26 strikes on Yemen capital, claim attack on Aramco facility in south of Riyadh • Trump’s top national security aides meet secretly on Yemen, Iran SANAA: Fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis showed no signs of abating on Saturday, with the Houthis saying the kingdom had launched dozens of strikes on capital Sanaa, while flames and smoke were seen rising from a facility belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco, south of Riyadh.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, Yonhap News Agency, The Hindu - International, Taipei Times, 3 hours ago: North Korea says test of intermediate-range strategic missile included use of AI.
North Korea said it tested an intermediate-range strategic missile on Saturday that involved the use of AI, hours after Seoul said Pyongyang had launched a ballistic missile. The launch took place days after Seoul’s military demanded an apology from Pyongyang for a blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) that it blamed on the North. Pyongyang has denied responsibility for last month’s explosion and called South Korea “despicable” on Friday, undercutting overtures by Seoul’s civilian leadership seeking a return to dialogue.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 17 hours ago: 11 terrorists killed during operations in KP, Balochistan: state media.
Security forces killed 11 terrorists during intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, state media reported on Saturday. State-run Radio Pakistan reported that five Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists had been killed during an IBO in KP’s South Waziristan district. Quoting security sources, the report said that security forces were continuing effective operations against Fitna al-Khawarij in KP under the Azm-i-Istehkam vision.
- The Hindu - International, 12 hours ago: Israeli strike kills five, including four women, in Gaza, health officials say.
Israel, which says Hamas has been rearming and launching attacks in violation of the ceasefire, ‌has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks
India - bottom line: Yemeni govt strikes Houthis as tensions rise amid reports of planned Saudi offensive.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Yemeni govt strikes Houthis as tensions rise amid reports of planned Saudi offensive.
Yemen's government has launched military strikes aimed at Houthi positions in Sanaa, marking a significant escalation amid the Houthis' recent announcement of a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia. As tensions rise, reports indicate that Saudi Arabia could unleash a major offensive against Houthi forces along the Red Sea coast, potentially mobilizing over 100,000 Yemeni troops depending on the operation's scale.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: 'Nihangs objected to clothing': Mystery surrounds LGBTQ+ influencer's killing.
Mad Sandhu, a well-known LGBTQ+ influencer and make-up artist, was shot dead in Amritsar. He was attacked while collecting his car after a wash on Loharka Road. Police have indicated they possess solid leads to identify the attackers and were investigating various angles for a motive. Previously, Sandhu faced objections from a Nihang group regarding his social media content and fashion choices.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: 'Divorce, Rs 30 lakh hospital bill': What led to techie's fatal jump from Supernova.
Sambhav Jain, a 28-year-old software engineer, died by suicide after jumping from a 41st-floor balcony. He had been staying alone in an Airbnb and expressed feelings of depression before the incident. Police are investigating personal difficulties and financial issues stemming from a recent divorce and medical expenses. Jain's father had suggested he return home to resolve a monetary dispute. The authorities are examining evidence, including CCTV footage and WhatsApp messages.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Hormuz blocked, but Gulf crude shipments at pre-war level.

- South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 4 hours ago: Houthis say they struck Aramco oil facility, as Saudis hit Sanaa.
Yemen’s Houthis claimed an attack on an oil facility near the Saudi capital on Saturday, where flames and smoke were seen, and accused the Gulf kingdom of striking Sanaa dozens of times. The foes have traded strikes since the Houthis seized all of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and took control of the Bab al-Mandab strait in a lightning offensive last month. Pakistani troops are expected to take over various defensive functions for Saudi Arabia to enable the Middle East country to fight an all-out war aimed at defeating Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels. According to defence analysts, Pakistani troops are not expected to participate directly in ground offensives against the Houthis being planned by Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s squabbling government factions. Instead, their primary objective would be to free up Saudi forces to focus on what is likely to...
- South China Morning Post - China, 16 hours ago: Chinese troops line up for Russia’s Tsentr-2026 exercise as military ties tighten.
Chinese troops have taken part in a mass multinational exercise in Russia featuring new anti-drone and ground robot systems – drills that Russian state media said “applied lessons” from the Ukraine war. The troops were among more than 47,000 military personnel involved in the Tsentr-2026 – or Centre-2026 – drills in the central western Chelyabinsk region from Monday until Saturday. From cooking and attending hospital visits to doing the actual quarrelling, paid “life stand-ins” are stepping in to manage these tasks, along with errands and awkward moments that many young Chinese would rather avoid. This trend, known as the “stand-in economy,” is gaining traction among time-strapped consumers who are willing to pay for convenience when daily responsibilities exceed their time, patience, or expertise.
